title: Harris' Conjecture
statement_text: The fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ can be upper bounded by a function (in fact, even a linear function) of the Hall ratio $\rho(G)$.
context_text: The Hall ratio $\rho(G) = \max_{H \subseteq G} |V(H)|/\alpha(H)$ is a natural lower bound for $\chi_f(G)$. Harris conjectured that the converse holds functionally; this question is also implicit in Johnson Jr [8]. The paper's abstract states it answers this question in the negative.
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture by establishing Corollary 3: for every positive integer $c$ there exists a graph with fractional chromatic number at least $c$ and Hall ratio at most $18$.
paper_title: 1-subdivisions, fractional chromatic number and Hall ratio

title: Blumenthal et al. Question 16
statement_text: Can the fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ be bounded by a fast-growing function of the Hall ratio $\rho(G)$?
context_text: Blumenthal et al. [2] showed that $\chi_f$ cannot be bounded by any polynomial in $\rho$, but their counterexample graphs still have unbounded Hall ratio, leaving open the possibility of a super-polynomial functional bound. The paper references this as [2, Question 16].
paper_contribution: Resolves the question negatively: Corollary 3 yields graphs with Hall ratio at most $18$ and $\chi_f$ arbitrarily large, so no function of $\rho$ alone can bound $\chi_f$.
notes: Not directly quoted; referenced as [2, Question 16] in the introduction.
paper_title: 1-subdivisions, fractional chromatic number and Hall ratio

title: Problem 4
statement_text: Determine the smallest function $g : \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ such that for every graph $G$, $\chi_f(G) \leq \rho(G)\,g(|V(G)|)$.
context_text: The Hall ratio of $G$ is $\rho(G)=\max_H |V(H)|/\alpha(H)$ over all subgraphs $H$ of $G$. For a weight assignment $w:V(G)\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$, $\alpha_w(G)$ is the maximum weight $w(Y)$ of an independent set $Y$; the fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ is the supremum of $w(V(G))/\alpha_w(G)$ over all weight assignments, and $\rho(G)$ is the same maximum restricted to $\{0,1\}$-valued weights, so $\rho(G)\le\chi_f(G)$. Harris conjectured that $\chi_f$ is bounded by a (linear) function of $\rho$; Blumenthal et al. showed it cannot be bounded by a polynomial. The authors answer the question negatively: for every $c$ there is a graph with $\chi_f(G)\ge c$ and $\rho(G)\le18$. This follows from two results on $1$-subdivisions (subdividing every edge once): every graph of average degree at least $256c^3$ ($c\ge10$) contains the $1$-subdivision of a graph of fractional chromatic number at least $c$, while for every $d$ there is a bipartite graph of average degree at least $d$ containing no $1$-subdivision of a graph with Hall ratio greater than $18$. For an $n$-vertex graph, repeatedly extracting a largest independent set gives $\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G)=O(\rho(G)\log n)$, so $g(n)=O(\log n)$ suffices. The graphs of fractional chromatic number at least $c$ and Hall ratio at most $18$ obtained by the authors have a number of vertices double exponential in their fractional chromatic number, which gives $g(n)=\Omega(\log\log n)$.
paper_title: 1-subdivisions, fractional chromatic number and Hall ratio

title: Problem 5
statement_text: Do there exist, for some constant $c > 0$, graphs $G$ of arbitrarily large fractional chromatic number such that $\rho(G) \leq c$ and $\alpha_{\deg_H}(H) \geq |E(H)|/c$ for every $H \subseteq G$?
context_text: The Hall ratio of $G$ is $\rho(G)=\max_H |V(H)|/\alpha(H)$ over all subgraphs $H$ of $G$. For a weight assignment $w:V(G)\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$, $\alpha_w(G)$ is the maximum weight $w(Y)$ of an independent set $Y$; the fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ is the supremum of $w(V(G))/\alpha_w(G)$ over all weight assignments, and $\rho(G)$ is the same maximum restricted to $\{0,1\}$-valued weights, so $\rho(G)\le\chi_f(G)$. Harris conjectured that $\chi_f$ is bounded by a (linear) function of $\rho$; Blumenthal et al. showed it cannot be bounded by a polynomial. The authors answer the question negatively: for every $c$ there is a graph with $\chi_f(G)\ge c$ and $\rho(G)\le18$. This follows from two results on $1$-subdivisions (subdividing every edge once): every graph of average degree at least $256c^3$ ($c\ge10$) contains the $1$-subdivision of a graph of fractional chromatic number at least $c$, while for every $d$ there is a bipartite graph of average degree at least $d$ containing no $1$-subdivision of a graph with Hall ratio greater than $18$. Here $\alpha_{\deg_H}(H)$ denotes $\alpha_w(H)$ for the weight assignment $w(v)=\deg_H(v)$, i.e. the maximum, over independent sets $Y$ of $H$, of the sum of the degrees in $H$ of the vertices of $Y$; note $\sum_v\deg_H(v)=2|E(H)|$. The authors ask more generally whether some natural non-trivial family $\mathcal{F}$ of weight functions, between $\{0,1\}$-valued weights (Hall ratio) and all weights (fractional chromatic number), gives a parameter $\rho_{\mathcal{F}}(G)=\max_{w\in\mathcal{F}}w(V(G))/\alpha_w(G)$ bounding $\chi_f$; since their lower bound on $\chi_f$ for the random graphs used in the $1$-subdivision theorem uses weights asymptotically proportional to degrees, degree weights are the first natural case to consider.

title: Problem 8
statement_text: Is it true that a class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded expansion if and only if there exists a function $f_6 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $G \in \mathcal{C} \mathbin{\triangledown} r$, $\rho(G) \leq f_6(r)$?
context_text: The Hall ratio of $G$ is $\rho(G)=\max_H|V(H)|/\alpha(H)$ over all subgraphs $H$ of $G$. A shallow minor at depth $r$ of $G$ is a graph obtained from $G$ by deleting vertices and edges and contracting pairwise vertex-disjoint subgraphs each of radius at most $r$; $\mathcal{C}\mathbin{\triangledown}r$ is the class of shallow minors at depth $r$ of graphs of $\mathcal{C}$. A class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded expansion if there is $f_1$ such that every graph of $\mathcal{C}\mathbin{\triangledown}r$ has average degree at most $f_1(r)$; equivalently, the maximum average degree, the colouring number, or the chromatic number of graphs in $\mathcal{C}\mathbin{\triangledown}r$ is bounded by a function of $r$. A class is nowhere dense if the clique number of graphs in $\mathcal{C}\mathbin{\triangledown}r$ is bounded by a function of $r$. The authors show (from the fact that graphs of average degree at least $256c^3$ contain the $1$-subdivision of a graph of fractional chromatic number at least $c$) that bounded expansion is also characterised by bounded fractional chromatic number $\chi_f$ in $\mathcal{C}\mathbin{\triangledown}r$. Since $\chi_f(G)\ge\rho(G)\ge\omega(G)$, bounded expansion implies the Hall-ratio property, which implies nowhere density; but the same argument fails for the Hall ratio, because there are graphs of arbitrarily large average degree containing no $1$-subdivision of a graph with Hall ratio greater than $18$. The authors also show a nowhere dense class with unbounded Hall ratio (from regular graphs of large girth and small independence number), and know no class with unbounded expansion whose shallow minors have bounded Hall ratio.
paper_title: 1-subdivisions, fractional chromatic number and Hall ratio
